docs/spec.md:6:A set of small 2D reinforcement-learning worlds (Snake, Fish tank, Predator-prey) built on one shared core: a world interface, a training loop, logging with learning-curve charts, a replay viewer, and baseline evaluation. In each world a hand-written learning agent is trained on a laptop, checked against random and rule-based play, watched in replays, and explained in a write-up. See the [brief](brief.md) for why.
docs/spec.md:14:**In scope:** World interface, Training runs, Run logging & learning curves, Replay viewer, Baseline evaluation, Reference check, World write-ups, Snake, Fish tank, Predator-prey.
docs/spec.md:30:**Behavior:** Every world presents the same face to the rest of the system: it can be reset from a seed, it reports what each agent observes as a short list of numbers, it accepts each agent's action, and it returns rewards, an end-of-episode signal and a world-specific score. It also describes its current state in a form the replay viewer can draw.
docs/spec.md:35:- **WORLD-02** Given the same seed and the same sequence of actions, a world produces the same sequence of observations, rewards and end signals.
docs/spec.md:36:  - Given a recorded episode's seed and actions, when they are replayed into a fresh world, then every observation, reward and end signal matches the recording.
docs/spec.md:37:- **WORLD-03** Each agent's observation is a fixed-length list of numbers, never an image.
docs/spec.md:38:  - Given any world, when an observation is taken at any step, then it has the same length as at every other step of that world and variant.
docs/spec.md:39:- **WORLD-04** A world declares its agents, the observation length and the action format (a choice from a fixed set, or a list of numbers within stated limits) before any episode starts.
docs/spec.md:40:  - Given any world, when the training loop asks for its description, then it receives the agent list, observation length and action format without running an episode.
docs/spec.md:46:  - Given a world with agents on two teams, when a step is taken, then each agent receives its own observation and reward, labelled with its team.
docs/spec.md:50:- An agent that has left the episode (e.g. a caught prey) is sent an action → the action is ignored and the agent receives no further observations that episode.
docs/spec.md:59:  - Given snake, its default settings, seed 1 and a budget of N steps, when the run is started, then it stops after exactly N environment steps.
docs/spec.md:89:  - Given 5 finished snake runs, when the chart is made, then it shows one mean line, one band, a random-play line and a rule-based line, with the axes labelled with the score name and "environment steps".
docs/spec.md:92:- **LOG-05** Each world can add its own logged measures (e.g. snake length at death, hits per fish), which are charted the same way as the score.
docs/spec.md:108:  - Given a snake run's 50% checkpoint and seed 7, when the replay is opened, then the episode plays from its first step to its end.
docs/spec.md:114:  - Given the 10% and 100% snake checkpoints and seed 7, when compared, then both start from the same board and advance one step at a time together; when one episode ends, its last frame stays while the other continues.
docs/spec.md:118:  - Given the rule-based snake and the final checkpoint on seed 7, when compared, then both play side by side as in REPLAY-04.
docs/spec.md:126:- A checkpoint from a world or variant whose observation length or action format no longer matches → the replay refuses to open and names the mismatch.
docs/spec.md:163:  - Given a hand-written snake mean of 18 food and a reference mean of 20, when checked, then it passes; at 15 against 20, it is flagged for investigation.
docs/spec.md:179:  - Given a new world, when it is set up, then its write-up starts with only the three part headings.
docs/spec.md:184:### Snake (`SNAKE`)
docs/spec.md:187:**Behavior:** The classic snake game on a square grid. The snake moves one cell per step, turns left, right or keeps going, grows when it eats food, and dies when it hits a wall or itself. The learner trains a snake that eats steadily and avoids itself, and watches it do so.
docs/spec.md:190:- **SNAKE-01** The world is a 10 × 10 grid with one snake starting 3 cells long in the middle, and one food item on a random free cell.
docs/spec.md:191:  - Given seed 3, when an episode starts, then the snake is 3 cells long near the center and one food item is on a cell the snake does not cover.
docs/spec.md:192:- **SNAKE-02** Each step the snake chooses one of three actions: turn left, turn right or go straight.
docs/spec.md:193:  - Given the snake heading up, when it turns left, then its head moves one cell left.
docs/spec.md:194:- **SNAKE-03** Eating food grows the snake by one cell, adds 1 to the score and places new food on a random free cell.
docs/spec.md:195:  - Given the head moves onto food, when the step ends, then the snake is one cell longer, the score is up by 1 and new food is on a free cell.
docs/spec.md:196:- **SNAKE-04** The episode ends when the head hits a wall or the snake's body, or after 100 steps without eating.
docs/spec.md:198:- **SNAKE-05** The score is the food eaten in the episode (higher is better).
docs/spec.md:200:- **SNAKE-06** The snake observes a fixed list of numbers: danger straight ahead, left and right; its heading; the food's direction relative to its head; and its length.
docs/spec.md:201:  - Given any step, when the observation is taken, then it has the same length and holds those values.
docs/spec.md:202:- **SNAKE-07** The rule-based baseline moves toward the food along the shorter axis, unless that move would end the episode next step, in which case it takes any move that does not.
docs/spec.md:204:- **SNAKE-08** The trained snake beats both baselines as in EVAL-04 and EVAL-05.
docs/spec.md:205:  - Given 5 finished snake runs, when evaluated, then both baselines are beaten.
docs/spec.md:208:- The snake fills every free cell → the episode ends as a win and the score counts all food eaten.
docs/spec.md:218:  - Given the ball heading into the right wall, when it touches the wall, then its sideways direction reverses and its speed is unchanged.
docs/spec.md:225:- **FISH-05** Variant "one fish": a single fish observes its own position and velocity and the ball's position and velocity.
docs/spec.md:226:  - Given the one-fish variant, when an observation is taken, then it holds those values for the fish and the ball.
docs/spec.md:227:- **FISH-06** Variant "many fish": 8 fish share the tank; each observes itself, the ball and the 3 nearest other fish.
docs/spec.md:228:  - Given the many-fish variant, when an observation is taken for any fish, then it holds its own state, the ball's and the 3 nearest fish's.
docs/spec.md:230:  - Given the ball beyond the radius, when a fish's observation is taken, then the ball's entries read "not seen".
docs/spec.md:237:- **FISH-11** Fish tank runs through the same training runs, logging, replay viewer and evaluation as snake, and snake's results reproduce unchanged after fish tank is added.
docs/spec.md:238:  - Given a snake run repeated with its original settings and seed after fish tank exists, when it finishes, then its results match the original run exactly.
docs/spec.md:260:- **PREY-06** Every agent observes itself, and the nearest 2 food pellets, nearest 2 prey and nearest 2 predators within a radius of one third of the arena's width; anything outside reads "not seen".
docs/spec.md:261:  - Given a predator beyond the radius, when a prey's observation is taken, then that predator's entries read "not seen".
docs/spec.md:270:- **PREY-11** Predator-prey runs through the same training runs, logging, replay viewer and evaluation as snake and fish tank, and their results reproduce unchanged after predator-prey is added.
docs/spec.md:271:  - Given a snake run and a fish run repeated with their original settings and seeds, when they finish, then their results match the originals exactly.

docs/architecture.md:8:Every world implements one multi-agent `World` protocol (AD-04): it resets from a seed, steps on one action array for all agents, and reports per-team scores and a drawable state. `train` drives a hand-written learner per team (AD-03) over a world for a fixed step budget. It plays held-out evaluation episodes through `core.play_episode` and writes everything to a run folder through `runlog` (AD-06). `evaluate` replays final checkpoints and both baselines on the final seeds and runs the paired permutation test. `charts` draws learning curves from run folders. `replay` re-simulates any checkpoint or baseline from a seed into a `Trace`, then shows it in a pygame window or writes it to MP4 (AD-07). `refcheck` trains Stable-Baselines3 on the same world through an adapter, kept away from every training run (AD-08).

docs/architecture.md:102:### AD-03: DQN for discrete actions, PPO for continuous ones, one learner per team
docs/architecture.md:104:- **Context:** Snake has 3 discrete actions (SNAKE-02); fish and predator-prey push with two numbers in [−1, 1] (FISH-02, PREY-02). Many-fish has 8 agents (FISH-06), and predator-prey has two teams learning at once (TRAIN-07). The brief wants each world to teach one idea, and wants checking against a reference implementation (CHECK-02).
docs/architecture.md:105:- **Decision:** `dqn` (replay buffer, target network, ε-greedy, Huber loss) for snake and the discrete check world. `ppo` (Gaussian policy, GAE, clipped objective) for fish, predator-prey and the continuous check world. All agents of a team share one learner (parameter sharing over a batch of agents). Teams have separate learners in the same run. Evaluation and replay act deterministically: greedy for DQN, the mean action for PPO.
docs/architecture.md:112:- **Decision:** `core.World` is a small protocol. Observations, actions, rewards and active masks are NumPy arrays indexed by agent, teams map to agent indices in `WorldSpec`, and `draw()` returns a `DrawState`. "Not seen" entries are a 0/1 flag followed by zeros, so lengths stay fixed (WORLD-03, FISH-07, PREY-06).
docs/architecture.md:147:- **Decision:** `train.run_check` trains each team method in a config on its check world: for DQN a 6-state corridor with two exits, left of state 0 (reward 0.8) and right of state 5 (reward 1.0), γ = 0.9, so the best action is left in states 0–1 and right in 2–5 and a learner biased to one action can't pass; for PPO a 1-D point that is rewarded for reaching a target, where the best push is the sign of the offset. It needs ≥ 95% agreement over every check-world state. `train.run_batch` runs the same check steps with the batch's method settings before starting any run and refuses the batch on failure. `rllab check <config>` runs it alone.

import numpy as np

from rllab.baselines.types import RulePolicy
from rllab.core import Array

# The snake's observation (SNAKE-06): danger after each action (0 straight, 1 turn left,

DANGER = slice(0, 3)
HEADING = slice(3, 7)
FOOD = slice(7, 11)

# Actions in the order the rule tries them, each with its quarter turns clockwise. Turning first
# moves the snake onto the other axis, closing the food's offset in a staircase.
MOVES = ((1, -1), (2, 1), (0, 0))


def choose(row: Array) -> int:
    """The first safe action toward the food; else the first safe action; else straight."""
    heading = int(np.argmax(row[HEADING]))
    food = row[FOOD]
    safe = [action for action, _ in MOVES if row[DANGER][action] == 0]
    toward = [action for action, turn in MOVES if action in safe and food[(heading + turn) % 4]]
    return (toward or safe or [0])[0]

    """Toward the food on the shorter axis, unless that move is fatal next step."""

            "unless that move would end the episode on the next step."
        )
